en: Majjhima Nikāya 143:
The Discourse of Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika.
Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika addressed a certain man:
“Come, good man, go to where the Blessed One is. Having approached him, pay homage with your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, saying:
‘Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’”
Go to where the Venerable Sāriputta is; having approached him, pay homage with your head at the feet of the Venerable Sāriputta in my name, saying:
"Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill;
he pays homage with his head at the feet of the Venerable Sāriputta."
“And speak thus:
‘It would be well, venerable sir, if the Venerable Sāriputta would approach the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika out of compassion.
“Very well, venerable sir,” that man replied to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika and went to where the Blessed One was.
He approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting there, that man said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill."
“...therefore he pays homage at the Blessed One’s feet with his head.
Then he approached the Venerable Sāriputta; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Sāriputta, he sat down to one side. Sitting there, that man said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:
“Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.”
Therefore, he pays homage at the feet of the Venerable Sāriputta with his head and says this:
“It would be well, venerable sir, if the Venerable Sāriputta would visit the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika out of compassion.”
The Venerable Sāriputta consented by remaining silent.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, with the Venerable Ānanda as his attendant monk, approached the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
He sat down on a seat. Having sat down, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:
"I hope you are bearing up, householder, I hope you are getting by. I hope your painful feelings are subsiding and not increasing, and that their subsiding is apparent, not their increase?
"Venerable Sāriputta, I am not bearing up, nor am I getting by. My painful feelings are severe; they are increasing and not subsiding, and their increase is apparent, not their subsiding."
"Venerable Sāriputta, it is just as if a strong man were to strike one on the head with a sharp spear; even so, venerable Sāriputta, violent winds are piercing my head.
It is neither bearable nor sustainable for me, venerable Sāriputta. My intense painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, not their subsiding."
"Venerable Sāriputta, it is just as if a strong man were to wrap a tight leather strap around my head; even so, venerable Sāriputta, I have an intense headache.
It is neither bearable nor sustainable for me, venerable Sāriputta. My sharp painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, not their subsiding.
Venerable Sāriputta, it is just as if a skilled butcher or a butcher’s apprentice were to use a sharp butcher’s knife..."
“...as if they were cutting his belly with a sharp knife; even so, venerable Sāriputta, violent winds cut my belly as if with a sharp knife.
It is not endurable for me, venerable Sāriputta, nor can I maintain myself. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, not their subsiding.
Just as if, venerable Sāriputta, two strong men were seizing a weaker man by both arms...”
“...and having taken them, they would heat them over a bed of glowing embers and burn them all around. Even so, venerable Sāriputta, there is an excessive burning in my body.
It is not bearable for me, venerable Sāriputta, nor can I endure it. My sharp painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, not their subsiding.”
“Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
‘I will not cling to the eye, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon the eye.
It is in this way, householder, that you should train yourself.”
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to the ear, and my consciousness shall not be dependent on the ear.
In this way, householder, should you train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to the nose, and my consciousness shall not be dependent on the nose.
It is in this way, householder, that you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to the tongue, and my consciousness shall not be dependent on the tongue.
It is in this way, householder, that you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to the body, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon the body.
It is in this way, householder, that you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to the mind, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon the mind.
It is in this way, householder, that you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to form, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon form.
It is in this way, householder, that you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
‘I will not cling to sounds… I will not cling to odors…’ [and so forth].
‘I will not cling to taste… I will not cling to tangible objects… I will not cling to mental phenomena,
and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon mental phenomena.’”
"In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
'I will not cling to eye-consciousness, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon eye-consciousness.'"
"In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
'I will not cling to ear-consciousness...'"
I shall not cling to nose-consciousness...
I shall not cling to tongue-consciousness...
I shall not cling to body-consciousness...
‘I shall not cling to mind-consciousness, nor shall my consciousness be dependent upon mind-consciousness.
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
‘I shall not cling to eye-contact, nor shall my consciousness be dependent upon eye-contact.
Thus, householder, should you train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way:
‘I will not cling to ear-contact...
I will not cling to nose-contact...
I will not cling to tongue-contact...’
‘I will not cling to body-contact… I will not cling to mind-contact, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon mind-contact.
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to feeling born of eye-contact, and my consciousness shall not be dependent on feeling born of eye-contact.
In this way, householder, should you train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to feeling born of ear-contact… I will not cling to feeling born of nose-contact…"
‘I will not cling to feeling born of tongue-contact… I will not cling to feeling born of body-contact… I will not cling to feeling born of mind-contact,
and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon feeling born of mind-contact.’”
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I will not cling to the earth element, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon the earth element."
"In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
'I shall not cling to the water element...'"
I shall not cling to the fire element...
nor shall I cling to the air element...
nor shall I cling to the space element...
‘I will not cling to the consciousness element, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon the consciousness element.
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
‘I will not cling to form, and my consciousness shall not be dependent on form.
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
‘I will not cling to feeling … I will not cling to perception … I will not cling to volitional formations …’
‘I will not cling to consciousness, nor will there be for me a consciousness dependent on consciousness.
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
‘I shall not cling to the base of infinite space, nor shall my consciousness be dependent upon the base of infinite space.
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:

‘I will not cling to the base of infinite consciousness… I will not cling to the base of nothingness… I will not cling to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.’
"In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
'I shall not cling to this world, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon this world.'"
In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
"I shall not cling to the world beyond, nor shall my consciousness be dependent upon the world beyond."
"In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
Therefore, householder, you should train yourself thus:
'Whatever has been seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, or pursued by my mind—that too I shall not cling to, and my consciousness shall not be dependent upon it.'"
“In this way, householder, you should train yourself.
When this was said, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika wept and shed tears.
Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:
“Are you lagging behind, householder? Are you sinking, householder?
“I am not lagging behind, venerable Ānanda, nor am I sinking;
however, for a long time I have attended upon the Teacher and upon the bhikkhus who are worthy of esteem.”
“Nor have I ever heard such a discourse on the Dhamma before.
“Householder, such a discourse on the Dhamma does not occur to those who are householders clothed in white;
rather, householder, such a discourse on the Dhamma occurs to those who have gone forth.”
“In that case, venerable Sāriputta, let such a Dhamma talk occur to white-robed householders as well.
For there are, venerable sir, sons of good family with little dust in their eyes who are declining through not hearing the Dhamma;
there will be those who understand the Dhamma.”
Then the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Ānanda, having exhorted the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with this instruction, rose from their seats and departed.
Not long after the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Ānanda had left, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika passed away and was reborn in the Tusita realm.
Then the young deva Anāthapiṇḍika, at the end of the night, having a most radiant appearance, [illuminated] the entire [park].
Having illuminated Jeta’s Grove, he approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the deva-son Anāthapiṇḍika addressed the Blessed One in verses:
“This indeed is that Jeta’s Grove, [which belongs to me, the son of Sudatta].”
Frequented by the community of seers,
inhabited by the King of Dharma,
it generates joy within me.
Action, knowledge, and the Dhamma,
and virtue as the supreme way of life—
by these mortals are purified.
Neither by lineage nor by wealth.
Therefore, a wise person,
clearly perceiving his own welfare, [should practice virtue].
Investigate the Dhamma with systematic reflection;
in this way, one is purified therein.
Sāriputta alone is supreme in wisdom.
“By virtue and by peace;
even a bhikkhu who has gone to the further shore would be at most only this much.”
Thus spoke the young deva Anāthapiṇḍika.
The Teacher gave his approval.
Then the young deva Anāthapiṇḍika:
“‘The Teacher approves of me,’ he said, and having paid homage to the Blessed One and circumambulated him, he vanished right there.
Then, at the end of that night, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
‘Bhikkhus, during this night, a certain son of the gods, with surpassing beauty, [approached].’”
Having illuminated the entire Jeta’s Grove, that son of the gods approached me; having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, that son of the gods addressed me in verse:
“This indeed is that Jeta’s Grove, [the resort of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus led by the Buddha].”
Frequented by the community of seers,
inhabited by the King of Dharma,
it generates joy within me.
Action, knowledge, and the Dhamma,
virtue as the supreme way of life—
by these mortals are purified.
Neither by lineage nor by wealth.
Therefore, a wise person,
seeing his own true welfare, [should practice virtue].
Investigate phenomena with systematic attention;
in this way, one is purified therein.
Sāriputta alone is supreme in wisdom.
“By virtue and by peace;
even a bhikkhu who has gone to the further shore could be no more than this.”
“Monks, that son of the gods said this.
Having paid homage to me, saying, ‘My Teacher approves,’ and having circumambulated me keeping me to his right, he vanished right there.
When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Surely, Bhante, that must have been the young deva Anāthapiṇḍika.
For the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, Bhante, was deeply devoted to the Venerable Sāriputta.
“Excellent, excellent, Ānanda!”
"Ānanda, whatever can be attained through reasoning has been attained by you.
Ānanda, that son of the gods is Anāthapiṇḍika.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
The Venerable Ānanda, elated, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.
The Discourse on the Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika is finished; it is the first.
